title: Customer Care Ruling: Limits, Charges and Credits Stay With Their Own Factory Production Order
content:
**Ruling.** When a customer holds several Factory Production Orders, every limit, charge and credit is figured per order and never pooled: guarantee credit caps, storage caps, hold counts and remake counts belong to the order they arise on. A guarantee credit is applied only to the contract its own order builds, never to another contract of the same customer. An order-level charge is owed on the order that incurred it and is never offset against a credit earned on a different order.

## What "per order" covers

| Item | Counted or capped on |
|---|---|
| On-time guarantee credit cap | the order that earned the credit |
| Storage fee cap | the order whose units are stored |
| Hold count | the order that was held |
| Remake count | the order whose units were remade |
| An earned guarantee credit | the contract that same order builds |
| An order-level charge (remake charge, expedite fee, storage fee) | the order that incurred it |

## Authority

The contract a guarantee credit may go to is read from the factory order record of the order that earned it — the window contract or door contract that order builds. A customer's statement about where a credit should go does not change that link.

## Hypothetical cases

- A customer has a window order and a door order. The window order earns a guarantee credit and the door order carries a storage fee. The credit goes to the window contract only; the storage fee stays owed on the door order and is not netted against the credit.
- A customer's first order has reached its hold count. A second order of the same customer keeps its own full hold allowance.
